components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Ember pill button, the system's default call-to-action.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #ff4514; color: #ffffff; font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 15px; padding: 12px 20px; border-radius: 9999px; border: none; transition: background 0.1s, transform 0.1s; } .ds-btn-primary:active { background: #d93a10; transform: scale(0.98); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #d93a10; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.4; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: White pill button with an Ink border, used alongside a primary Ember action.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: #ffffff; color: #141414; border: 2px solid #141414; font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 15px; padding: 10px 18px; border-radius: 9999px; transition: background 0.1s, transform 0.1s; } .ds-btn-secondary:active { background: #f9fafb; transform: scale(0.98); }

components.name: Status Chip
components.description: Fixed background/text pair per task status; never recolored ad hoc.
components.css: .ds-chip-done { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; background: #dcfce7; color: #15803d; font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 11px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 9999px; }

components.name: Dog Card
components.description: Tappable list row: neutral gray avatar block with the dog-face glyph (photo if available), name, breed/owner, next-stay pill.
components.css: .ds-card-dog { width: 100%; background: #fcfcfc; border: 1px solid #d1d1d1; border-radius: 22px; padding: 16px; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 16px; text-align: left; transition: transform 0.1s; } .ds-card-dog:active { transform: scale(0.98); } .ds-card-dog-avatar { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 64px; height: 64px; border-radius: 18px; background: #f3f4f6; } .ds-card-dog-name { display: block; font-family: Outfit, sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 20px; color: #141414; } .ds-card-dog-meta { display: block; font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 13px; color: #5c5c5c; margin-top: 2px; }

components.name: Bottom Nav
components.description: Flat Card-colored pill nav fixed to the bottom, separated from content by color alone.
components.html: TodayDogsCalendarSettings
components.css: .ds-bottom-nav { background: #f4f4ef; border-radius: 9999px; padding: 8px; display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr); } .ds-nav-item { flex: 1; text-align: center; padding: 10px; border-radius: 9999px; color: #78766e; font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; text-decoration: none; transition: background 0.15s, color 0.15s; } .ds-nav-item-active { background: #2344dd; color: #ffffff; font-weight: 700; }

narrative.overview: HeyPup is confident, capable, and a little proud of itself — the visual equivalent of a sitter who has three dogs fed, walked, and medicated before 9am and isn't stressed about it. The system reads bold and poppy (Ember coral against a crisp white canvas), but every playful choice — the Lottie dog mascot, the pill shapes — sits on top of a genuinely fast, glanceable task list. This is a working tool used mid-shift, one-handed, between a leash and a food bowl; it earns its warmth by staying legible under pressure, not by decoration alone. The system explicitly rejects the beige/neutral palette this app shipped with originally — that read as generic and "AI-built." It also rejects both directions a dog-care app could drift toward: clinical SaaS-blue dashboard chrome, and cartoon-kitsch pet-app cuteness that undermines trust in a tool people rely on for medication timing.
keyCharacteristics: One committed accent (Ember coral) carries all emphasis and status meaning — it is never "just decorative"
Flat, color-blocked surfaces; depth comes from scale-press feedback, not shadows
Pill shapes everywhere load-bearing touch happens: buttons, nav, chips, avatars
A warm, dog-forward voice (paw prints, a wagging mascot) kept in check by a display font with real gravity

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Ember is the only color that carries free-floating meaning (status, action, active state) outside the fixed task-type set (green/ember/blue/gray) — if a color starts meaning "done" or "urgent" on its own, that's a bug.

rules.name: The Avatar Rule
rules.body: Photo-less dog avatars are neutral: light gray (#f3f4f6) blocks with the Icon/dog face glyph in Ink Muted — never the paw icon, never a color. There is no pastel identity-accent bench.

rules.name: The Eyebrow Restraint Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracked labels are reserved for section headers and status metadata — never used as decorative kicker text above every block.

rules.name: The Flat Rule
rules.body: Depth cues come from a flatter/lighter background color (Card vs Studio White) and press feedback, never from shadows. No element in the system — including the bottom nav — carries a drop shadow.

dos: Do use Ember (#ff4514) as the only color that carries meaning — status, emphasis, active state.
Do keep surfaces flat; express depth with Card vs Studio White layering and active:scale press feedback, not shadows — except the floating bottom nav.
Do default to full pill shapes (rounded-full) for anything tappable: buttons, chips, nav, avatars.
Do keep uppercase tracked labels reserved for real section eyebrows and status chips, not decorative kickers.
Do reserve the Lottie dog mascot for loading/empty-state moments.
donts: Don't reintroduce a beige/cream/parchment-tinted background — the base surface is Studio White (#fcfcfc), a true near-white.
Don't drift toward clinical SaaS-dashboard chrome (cold blues/grays, dense data-table density).
Don't tip into cartoon-kitsch cuteness (mascot dominating a whole screen, baby-talk copy).
Don't color a dog avatar to signal status or identity — every photo-less avatar is the same neutral gray glyph.
Don't add drop shadows to inline cards or buttons — shadow is reserved for the floating bottom nav only.
